prompt: Implement Grover's search algorithm on 5 qubits using a REVERSED qubit-ordering convention relative to the standard grover_5q task: relabel every qubit index i used there as qubit (4-i). Under this relabeling, the two basis states marked by the standard task's oracle (|01101> and |10100>) become |10110> and |00101> respectively (read each string with qubit 4 as the leftmost bit, qubit 0 as the rightmost bit, same convention as the standard task) — find EITHER of these two marked basis states, using EXACTLY 3 Grover iterations (the optimal count for this problem size with 2 marked items). Use a pure PHASE oracle with no ancilla qubit: it must flip the sign (apply a -1 phase) of both |10110> and |00101>, and leave every other basis state unchanged. Each iteration is (oracle; diffuser), where the diffuser is the standard 'inversion about the mean' operator 2|s><s| - I (s = uniform superposition) — any correct gate decomposition of the diffuser is acceptable. Start from Hadamard on all 5 qubits, then apply 3 iterations. Return the resulting 5-qubit state; no measurement.
